posts:
Promises of housing clash with raw sewage in South Africa's North West.
Evidence: Unfinished homes, raw sewage, stalled funds
#Aletheia #Housing

Officials promise massive funding and housing fixes to restore dignity to neglected townships.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Trustworthy Good

Over 25,000 homes remain incomplete while millions vanish into stalled projects and flooded shacks.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.85, -0.8) — Severe Deception

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Broken housing promises leave impoverished families in squalor while public funds evaporate.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Housing Delivery: FAIL (-0.9, -0.8) — 25k homes left incomplete.
- Municipal Accountability: FAIL (-0.8, -0.8) — Sewage floods streets.
Thousands of government-funded homes in South Africa's North West province remain incomplete for years while families endure raw sewage and shacks.

The Poison:
Empty housing budgets mask deep administrative rot and contractor abandonment.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing political PR announcements (WHAT) with actual structural delivery to citizens (WHO).

Social Physics Analysis:
Officials run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by announcing rescue funds as a pretext, while systemic corruption and administrative failure leave vulnerable families stranded in raw sewage.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. F_pos and F_neg calculations confirm systemic regression.

The Unavoidable Truth: Millions are spent while vulnerable families remain trapped in squalor.

The Unavoidable Lie: Official announcements solve systemic housing failures.

Alethekanon:
Proclamations of rescue ring hollow when infrastructure rots in raw sewage. 🌐

Awwthekanon:
It breaks the heart to see mothers carrying toddlers through flooded streets of sewage while promised homes sit half-built for decades.

Brothekanon:
Another billion promised, but families are still living in shacks while the money disappears into thin air.

Spirithekanon:
"He who oppresses the poor to increase his wealth will comes only to poverty." Proverbs 22:16 PASS
False promises to the destitute bring ruin upon the community.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
R1-billion to fix North West’s failed housing projects

The province is sitting with roughly 25,400 unfinished homes

Actual Article Body:
This poorly built RDP home had its roof blown off during recent high winds in the township of Agisanang near Sannieshof in Tswaing Local Municipality, North West province.

Agnes Maropeng has lived in a corrugated iron shack for over 35 years in the informal settlement of Skierlek in Delareyville in the North West province.

Maropeng said her family and dozens of her neighbours in the beleaguered Tswaing Local Municipality have been promised housing, water and sanitation for decades.

Her street is flooded with raw sewage. The stench hangs over several blocks. “It is disgusting. I feel embarrassed living like this,” said Maropeng.

Carrying her toddler daughter on her back, she walks about three kilometres a day to collect water in buckets.

Agnes Maropeng has lived in a corrugated iron shack for over 35 years in the informal settlement of Skierlek.

Not far from Maropeng, Ganta Shey also lives in a corrugated iron shack without services alongside a half-built RDP house started over a decade ago.

How to solve Australia's housing crisis - ABC listen

“Will the Albanese government's faltering steps towards national leadership on housing turn into a confident stride or stagger to a halt?”

That’s the question asked in a new book by Matt Lloyd-Cape titled Our Place: How to Solve the Housing Crisis and Rebuild the Australian Dream, and it’s described as “An evidence-based guide... from a leading policy expert”.

Guest: Matt Lloyd-Cape is Senior Research Fellow at Per Capita and was the founding director of the Centre for Equitable Housing.
